title: Google Is Changing How It Bills for Missed Calls. Here's How to Stay Ahead of It.
summary: Google's Local Services Ads will start billing for missed calls and some follow-ups on Oct. 1. Here's the quick version, and how to make sure it never applies to you.
body_markdown:
Carey Landon


Product Marketing


Starting October 1, Google is changing how it bills Local Services Ads.


According to[reporting from Homepros](https://homepros.news/google-to-charge-for-some-missed-lsa-calls/) , missed calls during your listed business hours will now count as billable leads if the caller stays on the line more than 20 seconds. Qualifying follow-up calls can be billed too.


Google says the change is meant to cut down on spam and robocalls, rolling out across every vertical LSA supports, home services included.


## The short version for operators


A missed call used to be just a missed opportunity. Starting in October, it can also count as a billable lead.


**Responding consistently becomes critical.**


## Respond to every lead, no matter the channel


The best way to stay ahead of this is the same thing Google rewards: responding fast and responding always.


An LSA listing gives homeowners three ways to reach you, and Avoca now covers all three:


- **Call.**[Avoca's AI CSR](https://www.avoca.ai/inbound) answers every inbound call, instantly, 24/7. No gap during business hours for a missed-call charge to happen.
- **Quote request.**[Avoca's Speed-to-Lead](https://www.avoca.ai/speed-to-lead) responds the moment someone requests a quote, using Google's native GLSA messaging API. Google sees that response time and factors it into ranking, exactly the responsiveness this policy is designed to reward.
- **Book online.** Customers can now click “Book” right on your LSA listing and land in[Avoca’s Simple Scheduler](https://www.avoca.ai/simple-scheduler) . They see real availability and pick a time in the flow. Simple Scheduler already books at 3x the rate of legacy schedulers.


Consistently fast responses also improve your overall ranking in[Google's algorithm](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/6224859?hl=en) .


## The bottom line


You’re already paying for these leads. Under this update, how often you respond determines whether a lead is a booked job or a billable miss.


Avoca covers all three LSA channels at once, so every call, text, and booking request has the best shot at turning into a job.
